clauses.reason: The operative paragraph reads "I hereby exempt the said George Middleton from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1939." The exemption is a one-time permission for a fixed period and the period is stated in the order itself. By its own terms it runs through September 30, 1939, recorded inclusive under research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md; the exclusive reading ends it when September 30, 1939 begins. State on 2026-10-14: terminated, the permission having been exhausted by lapse of the stated period. Executive Order No. 8217, signed August 7, 1939, is a later event and not an end: its operative sentence reads "I hereby further exempt the said George Middleton from compulsory retirement for age for a period of six months ending March 31, 1940." It grants George Middleton a further exemption for six months ending March 31, 1940; it does not revoke or shorten this order, and under the owner ruling research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md an extension is recorded as a later event with its own date and quote.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 7978 of September 19, 1938, signed by Franklin D. Roosevelt, exempts George Middleton from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1939, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a). The held text is the American Presidency Project web transcription (APP node 210557, Common Crawl capture 2024-02-23T01:47:48Z); its page record in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl names Executive Order 7978, the date agrees with the text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file. The order is one whereas paragraph and one operative paragraph, so it is one clause. The exemption ends by its own terms on September 30, 1939; per research/readiness/owner_rulings/2026-10-21-until-and-further-exempt.md that day is recorded as the inclusive end, and the exclusive reading (the exemption stops when that day begins) is the alternative a reviewer should see. The packet records later extension order(s) No. 8217 (August 7, 1939); each is entered as a later event, and the machine search hits for this order (OFR catalog and held-text name search) are exactly those order(s).

savings.reason: The order grants a permission for a fixed period and contains no saving or transfer provision. What it left behind, George Middleton's continued federal employment during the period, accrued while the period ran; no duty or right continues after September 30, 1939 by the order's own terms. Any exemption after September 30, 1939 rests on the separate later order(s) recorded as later events.
